changes: Public configure-launch stages scope-bound local consent, protected references and optional approved provider home.
Public realize uses authenticated IPC; the owning daemon retains publication and serializes it with bootstrap rotation.
The daemon remains the inventory publisher. Realization verifies its authenticated path-free inventory and persists local evidence before HTTP.
Identical client intent replay recovers the same canonical realization after a lost response; no binding or runtime is implicitly created.
Cancelled IPC observers do not cancel publication; daemon shutdown drains owned work.
Registration revalidation tolerates inventory sequence advancement while preserving identity, profile and discovery-configuration fences.
Nexus returns a structured 403 for invalid realization tickets instead of an unhandled exception.

failure_history.finding: CLI inventory publication used a different producer on replay. Publication now remains with the automatic daemon.
failure_history.redaction: Ephemeral test bootstrap material was removed from the retained traceback.

failure_history.finding: Concurrent inventory sequence advancement conflicted with registration revalidation. Only that counter is excluded from the comparison; authority/configuration changes remain refused.
Independent CLI and daemon bootstrap refreshes revoked each other. Realization now runs inside the daemon under its bootstrap owner gate. Nexus also maps refusal to a structured HTTP response.

limitations: The TCP journey exercises public parsed CLI commands, actual authenticated local IPC, automatic daemon inventory and real Nexus HTTP routes. It seeds the imported identity and uses a technical vault.
The discovery candidate is a harmless copied interpreter, not an actual Codex provider. No provider is launched and no native/release qualification gate is overridden.
The realization ends PENDING_APPROVAL. Public binding prepare/apply, reusable runtime CLI mapping and real remote provider journeys remain pending.
Bootstrap realization uses the registration identity as required by the current scoped bootstrap contract; this is not full multi-agent onboarding acceptance.
